title: Entity-page tools in the admin portal: filters, columns, grouping, entity drawers, saved views, third-party tickets and formatting rules

prose.label: Saved views.
prose.text: {{saved-view-pages}} The saved-view page's AEM list and the Users page disagree about saved views on AEM > Users {{divergence:aem-users-saved-views}}. The entity lists otherwise differ between the grouping, drawer and saved-view pages {{gap:entity-list-differences}}. {{saved-view-dashboards}} {{saved-view-content}}

filter-scope.statement: Filtering fields depend on the page: dashboards with data from several entities filter by dimensions but not measurements, while entity pages typically filter by both; filter options vary by field type and by whether the field is repeated, and applied filters reset when you leave the page.

quotes: dashboards with data from multiple entities support filtering by dimensions but not measurements, while entity pages typically allow filtering by both
Different fields have filtering options that vary according to the field type (e.g., Boolean, Text, Number, Date, IP) and whether it can contain multiple values (i.e., repeated fields).
Applying filters adjusts the displayed data to what is included in the filter's scope. This resets when you leave the page.

filter-repeated-list.statement: Selecting values in the list filter of a repeated field returns records containing at least one of them, which works like the Equals (Any) operator.

quotes: selecting one or more values returns records containing at least one of the selected values
functions similarly to the Equals (Any) operator in conditional filtering

filter-repeated-conditional.statement: Conditional filters on repeated fields can be checked against any or all of the field's values, except Is Empty and Is Not Empty, which are Boolean filters on the field as a whole with no All or Any variation.

quotes: you can specify whether the filter should be checked against any or against all the field's values
The Is Empty and Is Not Empty operators are Boolean filters and do not have All or Any variations.
these operators apply to the field as a whole, making the distinction between All and Any unnecessary.

filter-clearing.statement: Clear Selection empties one filter's values, deselecting it in More removes it from the filters bar, and Clear All Filters removes all active filters.

quotes: click the field in the filters bar and click Clear Selection
click Clear All Filters
To remove a field from the filters bar, open the More drop-down menu and deselect the field from the list of active filters.

columns.statement: Table columns (measurements and dimensions) are added, removed and ordered in the Manage Table Columns window (in-use list and available list), sorted by clicking a header, and restored with Reset to Default followed by Apply.

quotes: which include measurements (quantitative fields) and dimensions (categorical fields)
displaying columns currently in use on the right, and columns that can be added on the left
To undo the changes and revert to the default display, click Reset to Default and then click Apply.
In the IN USE list, drag the columns in the order you want them to appear.
To sort a table by a column, click the column header you want to sort by.

grouping-pages.statement: Grouping of entity pages is available for UVM Tickets, Assets, Findings and Exceptions; AEM Assets, Violation Tickets, Policy Violations and Users; Agentic SOC Incidents, Alerts, Assets and Users; and Identity Protection Users, Identity Findings, Tenants and Alerts.

quotes: Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM): Tickets, Assets, Findings, and Exceptions
Asset Exposure Management (AEM): Assets, Violation Tickets, Policy Violations, and Users
Agentic SOC: Incidents, Alerts, Assets, and Users
Identity Protection: Users, Identity Findings, Tenants, and Alerts

grouping-behaviour.statement: Grouping creates collapsible sections by the chosen field and is removed with Clear Selection; grouping preferences can be saved in a saved view.

quotes: Grouping your view creates collapsible sections based on the field you select.
click Clear Selection at the bottom of the Group By drop-down menu
Your grouping preferences can be saved as a set view.

drawer-pages.statement: Entity drawers can be configured under Settings > UI Config for UVM Tickets, Assets, Findings and Exceptions; AEM Assets, Violation Tickets, Policy Violations and Users; Agentic SOC Incidents, Alerts, Assets and Users; and Identity Protection Users, Identity Findings, Tenants and Alerts.

quotes: In the left-side navigation, click Settings > UI Config.
Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM): Tickets, Assets, Findings, and Exceptions
Asset Exposure Management (AEM): Assets, Violation Tickets, Policy Violations, and Users
Agentic SOC: Incidents, Alerts, Assets, and Users
Identity Protection: Users, Identity Findings, Tenants, and Alerts

drawer-types.statement: A drawer is configured per entity and type (for UVM tickets the example types are CVE, DEFAULT and MISCONFIG); Save as New Type uses an existing type as the template and leaves the original types unaffected, and Severity and Status Timeline checkboxes show those items in the drawer's top panel.

quotes: (e.g., CVE, DEFAULT, MISCONFIG for the Ticket drawer in UVM)
Select the Severity checkbox to display the severity level in the top panel of the entity drawer.
Select the Status Timeline checkbox to display the status timeline in the top panel of the entity drawer.
use it as a template to create a new type. The original types are not affected.
From the Entity drop-down menu, select the entity drawer you want to configure
Click Save as New Type to save the settings as a new type.

drawer-tabs.statement: System drawer tabs can be rearranged, extended with fields, deleted and restored (the Details tab can place fields in a left or right column); custom tabs can additionally be edited but a deleted custom tab cannot be restored.

quotes: | System Tabs | Rearrange tabs by dragging them to a new position. Add new fields. Delete tabs. Restore deleted tabs. For the Details tab, you can specify whether fields appear on the left or right columns. Configure data as fully visible or revealed only when expanding the respective table row (Visible/On Expand). |
Delete tabs (cannot be restored later).

saved-view-pages.statement: Saved views exist on entity pages (UVM Tickets, Findings, Assets, Exceptions; AEM Assets, Violation Tickets, Policy Violations; Agentic SOC Incidents, Assets, Alerts, Users; Identity Protection Users, Tenants, Identity Findings, Alerts), on named system dashboards, and when viewing items in a dashboard widget.

quotes: Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM): Tickets, Findings, Assets, and Exceptions
Asset Exposure Management (AEM): Assets, Violation Tickets, and Policy Violations
Agentic SOC: Incidents, Assets, Alerts, and Users
Identity Protection: Users, Tenants, Identity Findings, Alerts
When viewing items in a dashboard widget
System dashboards

saved-view-dashboards.statement: The system dashboards that support saved views are UVM Overview, Remediation History, Risk, Explore Vulnerabilities and Asset Coverage; AEM Policy Compliance, Asset Inventory and Tool Coverage And Gap; the Agentic SOC SOC Workbench Dashboard; and Identity Protection Critical Findings and Findings Overview.

quotes: UVM: Overview, Remediation History, Risk, Explore Vulnerabilities, and Asset Coverage
AEM: Policy Compliance, Asset Inventory, and Tool Coverage And Gap
Agentic SOC: SOC Workbench Dashboard
Identity Protection: Critical Findings and Findings Overview

saved-view-content.statement: A saved view stores filters, grouping, sorting and field selections; accounts come with system-saved views for common use cases, and views can be reset to default, favorited, created, edited and deleted.

quotes: Saved views are configurable, reusable views that apply filters, grouping, sorting, and field selections to data.
Your account is equipped with system-saved views, which are configured to reflect common use cases.
Reset the Default View
Add Favorite Views
Create a New View
Edit Views
Delete Views

third-party-bulk.statement: Tickets can be sent to an external work-management system one at a time from the ticket drawer or in bulk with Create 3rd Party Issue (one external ticket per platform ticket), but not in bulk to different outegrations such as Jira Bugs and Jira Tasks.

quotes: In the ticket drawer, click Create <Vendor> Ticket.
Click Create 3rd Party Issue.
A separate external ticket is created for each Agentic SecOps Platform ticket.
Agentic SecOps Platform tickets cannot be dispatched in bulk to different outegrations (e.g., Jira Bugs and Jira Tasks).

third-party-link.statement: An existing external ticket is linked with Manually connect by entering only its ticket ID (for example INC0012345), not its URL; one third-party ticket can link to only one platform ticket.

quotes: select Manually connect <Outegration>
Enter only the third-party ticket ID (e.g., INC0012345 for a ServiceNow ticket ID), not the ticket's URL or link.
A third-party ticket can only be linked to one Agentic SecOps Platform ticket.

third-party-sync.statement: With two-way sync configured, creating or linking a third-party ticket triggers the sync and updates the platform ticket per the outegration settings; after unlinking, updates no longer sync.

quotes: After the tickets are unlinked, updates between the third-party ticket and the Agentic SecOps Platform ticket no longer sync.

If two-way sync from the external system to the Agentic SecOps Platform is configured, creating a third-party ticket triggers the sync and updates the Agentic SecOps Platform ticket based on the outegration's settings.

If two-way sync from the external system to the Agentic SecOps Platform is configured, linking a third-party ticket triggers the sync and updates the Agentic SecOps Platform ticket based on the outegration's settings.

third-party-filter.statement: Tickets can be filtered by link state using the Ticket External Issue Type field (select integrations) or adding the Empty field to display tickets with no linked third-party ticket.

quotes: add the Ticket External Issue Type field to the filters and select the desired integrations, or add the Empty field to display tickets with no linked third-party tickets

formatting-numeric.statement: Numeric formatting rules apply a colour to a measurement by operator and threshold (Between needs a start and end value) and are evaluated top to bottom, with the top condition winning where conditions overlap.

quotes: Numeric rules allow you to define custom coloring rules for measurements.
The Between operator requires both a starting and ending value for the numerical range.
Numeric rules are evaluated in the order they appear (from top to bottom). When there is an overlap between conditions, the color of the top condition takes priority.

formatting-dimension.statement: Dimension-based formatting rules colour dimension values: rules can be configured for the top 25 dimension values, the page says this rule applies only to pie, bar, and table charts, and repeated fields are not currently supported.

quotes: Dimension-based rules allow you to define custom coloring rules for dimensions.
Rules can be configured for the top 25 dimension values.
This rule applies only to pie, bar, and table charts.
Repeated fields are not currently supported.

formatting-fallback-apply.statement: A rule's fallback is either Back to Default or a Customize colour for values that meet no condition; rules are created under Configure > Formatting Rules and can be applied to custom dashboard widgets (Style tab) and to AEM compliance policies; the AEM procedure is written for a numeric rule.

quotes: Back to Default: Restores the default color assigned to the rule.
Customize: Select a color for values that do not meet the conditions.
go to Configure > Formatting Rules
You can apply formatting rules to compliance policies or custom dashboards.
To apply a formatting rule (numeric rule) to an Asset Exposure Management (AEM) policy:
Click the Style tab.
In the Formatting Rule section, select the relevant formatting rule.
Click Save to apply the rule to the policy.

entity-list-differences.title: Why the grouping, drawer and saved-view pages list different entities
entity-list-differences.detail: The saved-view page adds system dashboards that the grouping and drawer pages do not list. Apart from AEM Users (see the divergence), no captured page says whether an entity missing from a page's list is unsupported there.

aem-users-saved-views.summary: The saved-views page lists AEM entities Assets, Violation Tickets and Policy Violations without Users, while the About Users page offers system-saved and saved views on AEM > Users.

positions.says: Saved views exist for AEM Assets, Violation Tickets and Policy Violations; Users is not listed.

quotes: Asset Exposure Management (AEM): Assets, Violation Tickets, and Policy Violations

positions.says: On the Users page (including AEM > Users) you can select from system-saved views or views you previously saved.

quotes: On the Users page (Agentic SOC > Users, Identities > Users, or AEM > Users)
Select from system-saved views or views you previously saved.

aem-users-saved-views.impact: Whether saved views are available on AEM > Users depends on which page is right.
